chapter: Parker, Buster Smith and the Kansas City style
title: Lunceford, Claude Hopkins and McKinney's Cotton Pickers rhythm sections
summary: Lunceford's section had a churchy feel; Hopkins and McKinney's Cotton Pickers also swung.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, I just want -- I don't want to sidetrack, but I'm just interested in the rhythmic thing here. Now, let's just think a minute, well, now, how about a rhythm section like Lunceford's?
Lunceford's was very good. It was --
I don't mean those up-tempo things, when they're doing their sort of two-beat meters.
Yeah. They were very good, and I would
say they were the first movement towards that churchy feeling.
Yeah.
Like, (singing "Mary").
Yeah, that's churchy, too, really.
Yeah, that's churchy, but it's only churchy from what the rhythm section is doing, because the horns were playing in a very unique style, and that was arrangements.
Yeah, yeah.
But it showed that there was relaxation in what they played, like Tommy Dorsey's --
"Yes" / Indeed?
Didn't Dorsey make Remember?
That was Lunceford's band.
No, that was Lunceford's band. Remember, (singing). Dorsey had something just like that.
Well, maybe so.

I don't know whether it was "Remember." was so related. In your sleep you'd still be patting your foot. Anyway, it was something like that. It (unintelligible) those Yeah, those rhythm sections, Lunceford and all those bands that became prominent usually had good swinging rhythm sections.

Yeah. Well, there was another one that I liked, at one time, Claude Hopkins had a nice rhythm section, where he had -- I can't remember the drummer's name, but he was good. Jacobs, I think his name was. That was a very nice,
soft rhythm sound.
Yeah, I remember that coming from the Roseland. I used to hear them -- I didn't know them too well, but they moved.
Yeah.
I'm trying to think of that thing that Don Redman had. Who was it had Cuban Austin or somebody like --
Well, Cuban Austin was in McKinney's Cotton Pickers.
That was the band.
Yeah.
They came out to Kansas City in the Midwest and tore it up. That was --
When was that?

That was, I think, around the time -- but they were just passing through. But -- no, that was before. That was before I got (unintelligible). Yeah, they came all out in Texas and everything. They were supposed to be from Michigan or somewheres.
Yeah. Was Don Redman with them then?
Yeah.
Oh, because that was a good band then.
Yeah, they was spanking them. That's where I got Don and Cuba (unintelligible) associated.
